payload.choice_traced: The winner - fragment-carried key, ciphertext plus inline decryptor in one page, confirm-then-announce, degrade-and-record, absolutize the answer URL at send time, and push exactly when the run would wait - traces to five criteria each carrying its requirement lineage: C1 the owner is reached (R1, R8, R9, Q1, VETO), C2 readable (R4, R6), C3 the host learns nothing (R5, R11), C4 failure visible (R8, R12), C5 no new dependency surface. ONE Pugh run is recorded, with the shipped lane as datum rather than a hypothetical. The datum fails TWO veto criteria - its action URL cannot be tapped, and it publishes nothing when the pairing changed after startup - so the outcome is disqualification, not a score. No second run exists, recorded as the deliberate strike it is: all twelve alternatives were eliminated at M5 on stated failures, and the architecture itself is ruled by se-v2-design §11/§18 and by v1's implementation.
payload.sensitivity_ruled: VERDICT: robust to weights - two veto failures cannot be reweighted away - and vulnerable to three environment shifts, all now RAID tripwires. se.raid-brief-exports-evidence-content (risk, OWNER): the brief carries evidence verbatim, which is fine while evidence is ledger prose and stops being fine the moment no-remote or credential-bearing material reaches an evidence field; the fallback is a tier filter or dropping to the actions-only rung, recorded now so it is owed work rather than a surprise. se.raid-phone-app-rendering-drifts (risk, agent): a third-party app change would degrade the rung with no server-side symptom, and the floor is the two direct actions. se.raid-action-budget-binds (assumption, agent): all three slots are spent, so bless-with-changes will push choice-making onto the page, which is what v1 already does.
payload.matrix_review: KILLER - the baseline reviewed as data. DECOMPOSITION: four elements plus two standing constraints - E1 the gatekeeper, E2 the brief pipeline, E3 the summons, E4 the answer reader, with report-the-attempt and withhold-the-credential sitting over them rather than inside them. CLUSTERING: the tear is between E2 and E3, justified by failure mode rather than tidiness - E2 exists to be allowed to fail, E3 exists to fire regardless. ALLOCATION: fifteen functions, fifteen allocations, each exactly once; the one that could have been double-allocated is F12 degrade-deliberately, and it sits with E2 because the DECISION to continue without a brief belongs to E2's contract of never failing outward, while E3 merely receives an absent input. INTERFACES: three, each declared at both ends. I1 (permission and pairing) is mandatory. I2 (the brief URL) is OPTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION and is the only such interface in the design - that single edge IS the ladder. I3 (the answer topic) is symmetric because both ends derive it from the same pairing through the same absolutization rule, and it is worth naming that this symmetry is exactly what was broken before: the card wrote a scheme-like token while the reader expected a topic. No element reaches inside another - E3 never asks why E2 returned nothing, E2 never learns whether a card was sent. No new element was needed during probing, so nothing returns to this gate.
payload.evaluation_recorded: Q1 reachability: ADDRESSED, carried by se.adr-ladder-degrades-loudly and I2's optionality. ONE RESIDUE FLAGGED rather than claimed: if E3's own publish fails, the owner receives nothing and only the record shows it - the scenario is then satisfied by 'a recorded failure' rather than by delivery, which is the honest ceiling of a single channel, and a second channel is deliberately out of scope. Of the five tensions: three addressed, one (mockable versus tappable) UNADDRESSED BY CONSTRUCTION and correctly so - it becomes D1, a real tap, because no matrix can settle it - and one (free-tier versus expectation) addressed by degradation with its own tripwire. Deliberately unaddressed: filtering brief content by tier, which needs kb's tiering to exist first and is recorded as RAID.
payload.adrs_traced: Every deciding ADR addresses the requirement that forced it: se.adr-absolute-action-urls -> R1; se.adr-brief-encrypted-fragment-key -> R4, R5; se.adr-verify-before-announce -> R6; se.adr-ladder-degrades-loudly -> R8, R12, Q1; se.adr-announce-by-adjudicator -> R9, R10, and it is the only one adjudicated by the owner. That last one was RESTATED at the owner's correction during this milestone, because my paraphrase was loose: the test is not who owns the decision but whether the agent would otherwise WAIT - a gate the agent will bless itself pushes nothing, a gate the run is about to park on always pushes. The build's R9 check follows that wording exactly.
